The '''2017 Supercopa de España''' was the 34th edition of the [[Supercopa de España]], an annual two-legged [[Association football|football]] tie contested by the winners of the previous season's [[La Liga]] and [[Copa del Rey]] competitions.

The tie was played in August 2017 between the winners of the [[2016–17 Copa del Rey]] and holders of the Supercopa, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], and the champions of the [[2016–17 La Liga]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. This was the first time since the [[2012 Supercopa de España|2012 edition]] that the Supercopa featured [[El Clásico]].

Real Madrid won the Supercopa de España 5–1 on aggregate for their 10th title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/08/16/real-madrid-vs-barcelona-spanish-super-cup-live-score-updates/|title= Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 0 (5-1 on aggregate): Woeful Barca dismissed as Zinedine Zidane's unstoppable side win Super Cup|date=17 August 2017|work=Telegraph|access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref>

==Match details==
===First leg===
The first half of the match ended goalless. Five minutes into the second half, [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] fired a ground cross that deflected off [[Gerard Piqué|Piqué's]] foot, resulting in an [[own goal#Association football|own goal]]. Four minutes later, Real Madrid had a great opportunity to score when Benzema did a stepover and evaded Pique's tackle, then sent a cross to [[Dani Carvajal]] across the goal and Carvajal shot but [[Jordi Alba]] cleared it on the goal line. In the 70th minute, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] scored after a pass from [[Casemiro]] but it was ruled offside. Seven minutes later, [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] was brought down in the box by [[Keylor Navas]], resulting in a penalty, which was subsequently converted by [[Lionel Messi|Messi]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2017/aug/13/barcelona-v-real-madrid-spanish-super-cup-first-leg-live|title= Barcelona 1-3 Real Madrid: Spanish Super Cup, first leg – as it happened|date=13 August 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-08-14|title=Barcelona 1 - 3 Real Madrid: as it happened, goals, match report|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/08/13/football/1502613292_718396.html|access-date=2020-10-15|website=AS.com|language=en|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020055355/https://en.as.com/en/2017/08/13/football/1502613292_718396.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Messi's strike marked his 25th goal in the fixture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/social-networks-leo-messi-and-luis-suarez-call-for-optimism|title=Leo Messi and Luis Suárez call for optimism|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 August 2017|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref> Three minutes later, in the 80th minute, Real scored their second through a counter attack when [[Isco]] assisted Ronaldo with a long ball who shot into the top right corner from the edge of the box. Ronaldo was booked for removing his shirt as part of the celebration. Two minutes later he was booked again by the referee for allegedly diving when he collided with [[Samuel Umtiti]] in the box, which resulted in a second yellow card to become a [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)#Red card (dismissal)|red card]], therefore getting suspended for the second leg. Ronaldo was later given a five-match suspension after replays showed him push the referee in frustration for the red card. Real's last goal was scored in the 90th minute in similar fashion to the second, when [[Marco Asensio|Asensio]] shot into the top left corner following an assist from [[Lucas Vázquez]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-1-3-real-madrid-to-be-continued... |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |title=FC Barcelona 1-3 Real Madrid: To be continued... |date=13 August 2017 |access-date=13 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029152757/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-fc-barcelona-1-3-real-madrid-to-be-continued... |archive-date=29 October 2017 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/08/1-3-a-real-madrid-exhibition-at-the-camp-nou|title=1-3: A Real Madrid exhibition at the Camp Nou {{!}} Real Madrid CF|work=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=13 August 2017|title=Barcelona vs. Real Madrid - Football Match Report|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=479398|access-date=15 October 2017|website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Second leg===
The first goal came quite early in the second leg through a Real throw-in the fourth minute following a poor clearance from Samuel Umtiti which resulted in the ball landing in the young [[Marco Asensio]]'s feet who scored from 30+ yards out with his left foot.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2017/aug/16/real-madrid-barcelona-spanish-super-cup-second-leg-live|title= Real Madrid 2-0 Barcelona: Spanish Super Cup, second leg – as it happened|date=17 August 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=24 August 2017}}</ref> In the 32nd minute, Benzema stole the ball from [[Javier Mascherano]] and passed it to Lucas Vazquez in the center of the box who then hit the left post. 

Eight minutes after the half-hour mark, [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] sent a ground cross in for [[Karim Benzema|Benzema]] who controlled it backwards with his right foot and finished with a left foot half-volley straight into the bottom corner of the net which was enough for the victory. Six minutes after the start of the second half, [[Raphaël Varane]] made a poor pass to [[Mateo Kovačić]] to let Suarez recover the ball and pass it to Messi who then hit the crossbar inside the box. In the 70th minute, [[André Gomes|Andre Gomes]] took a throw in and played it to Suarez who then made a body feint and dribbled past [[Dani Carvajal]]. Suarez then played a through ball to [[Sergi Roberto]] on the left side of the box who toe poked the ball, which was saved by Navas. Varane's header fell to [[Ivan Rakitić|Ivan Rakitic]] a few yards outside the box who then passed the ball to Messi who took a shot, which was saved by Navas, and the deflection fell in the path of Suarez who performed a diving header that bounced off the right side post and went out of play.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 August 2017|title=Real Madrid outclass Barcelona for Spanish Super Cup crown|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=479397|access-date=2020-10-14|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

There was lesser action for the last 20 minutes, although [[Théo Hernandez]], [[Dani Ceballos]] and [[Nélson Semedo]] came on to make their official debuts respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/match-report-real-madrid-2-0-fc-barcelona-super-cup-slips-away|title=Real Madrid 2-0 FC Barcelona: Super Cup slips away {{!}} FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|language=en-US|access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=17 August 2017 |title=Real Madrid-Barcelona: 2-0: Spanish Super Cup Champions! |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/08/2-0-spanish-super-cup-champions |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180109111530/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/08/2-0-spanish-super-cup-champions |archive-date=9 January 2018 |access-date=17 August 2017 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>
